returns.x_m: not returned, grader integrates from yaw_rate + measured v
returns.y_m: not returned, grader integrates from yaw_rate + measured v

manifest.model: Steady-state understeer-corrected single-track: psi_dot = v * tan(delta) / (L + K_us * v^2); K_us = (m/L) * (l_r/Cf - l_f/Cr).
manifest.parameter_source: openpilot-canonical ST parameters mirrored from code/parameters.py (m, L, l_f, l_r, C_alpha_f, C_alpha_r).
manifest.calibration: none. Hooks STEER_BIAS_RAD and STEER_LAG_S provided for future per-platform empirical tuning, both initialised to 0.
manifest.methodology_summary: V0 baseline is pure kinematic single-track (psi_dot = (v/L) tan delta). V0 over-predicts yaw rate at speed in turns because it ignores tyre slip. V1 replaces V0 with the steady-state cornering relation derived from the linear-bicycle lateral dynamics in the high-grip limit; the denominator L + K_us*v^2 grows with speed^2 and reduces predicted yaw exactly where V0 leaves residual. K_us is positive for all three openpilot platforms (mild understeer). Implementation keeps tan(delta) (rather than delta) for graceful behaviour at large rack angles, and zeros yaw below v=0.5 m/s. x_m/y_m are intentionally not returned so the grader integrates from this yaw using the same measured velocity it already has.
limitations_self_reported: Harness blocked all python execution, so V1 was not scored against V0 on the truth pool. Direction of effect is known a priori from K_us > 0.
STEER_BIAS_RAD and STEER_LAG_S were not fit and remain at 0.
Symlinks data/ and code/ were not created because ln -s was also denied; predict.py is self-contained and does not depend on either.
